label: Tharparkar

names.text: Names as listed on the Wikipedia page.

about.text: A dual-purpose desert breed from Tharparkar District in Sindh, Pakistan, also found in India. It is medium-sized and light grey, with a white stripe along the backbone, and is adapted to scarce feed. It is used for milk and for draught work.

sources.text: Summarised from the Wikipedia page, which cites Khan & Isani (1994), p. 59, for the habitat and physical details.

origin.place: Tharparkar District, Sindh, Pakistan; also found in India

sources.text: Origin place as stated on the Wikipedia page. No year of formation or first record is given there.
Listed as dual-purpose, for milk and draught work, on the Wikipedia page.

facts.v: Tharparkar District has large sand dunes, and grazing is adequate only a few months after the monsoon rains (July to September).

sources.text: From the Habitat section of the Wikipedia page, citing Khan & Isani (1994), p. 59.

facts.v: Adult males weigh 400 to 500 kg and females 300 to 380 kg.

sources.text: From the physical traits section of the Wikipedia page.

gaps: Looked for milk yield per lactation and lactation length; a Wikipedia page gives only 'fairly good milk producers', and web search snippets gave research-herd figures (roughly 1,500 to 2,000 kg per lactation) that were not fetched from their papers, so none is recorded. No population figure, year of formation, milk composition, or FAO/DAD-IS risk status was found on the Wikipedia page.
